content.comment_body: The program I created is fairly basic, but since I'm new to this, I hope my questions aren't too obvious. I’ve included a screenshot from the ABB software for reference. [snip] Here’s my progress in [product_name]: [snip] I’m struggling to figure out how to add branches to the upper ladder in [product_name]. Also, is there a straightforward way to make timer values adjustable directly from the PLC’s LCD panel?
Hello [user_name], Welcome to the forum! Please check the attached video for guidance.
Thanks so much, I appreciate your help. Do you know how to allow timer values to be set as variables so they can be changed through the PLC’s LCD?

Create one or more message texts in your configuration. Within these messages, include the timer parameters you want to be editable. Refer to the attached diagram for visual guidance. To update a parameter, select the relevant message text. Press and hold the ESC key for over 2 seconds; a black bar will then appear in the input/output field. Use the up/down cursor keys to move between different fields. Once you choose the field to modify, press OK (on TDE, that’s Enter). The black bar changes to a blinking box; now, adjust the value with the up/down keys or reposition with left/right keys. When done, press OK again to return to the black bar. You can continue adjusting other fields or press ESC to exit the operation.

This approach displays the timers on the main LCD screen, which helps, but when editing 'parameters' via the LCD, they still appear as generic codes like 'b001'. Is there a way to give these a more recognizable name? Field technicians would find it easier to see labels like 'Timer 1' and 'Timer 2'.
What issue are you facing? For example, in the first row of the message text, you can place a name such as 'Timer1' on the left and the corresponding parameter field on the right.
